title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM-Generated NetOps Artifacts: a Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to measure how much automated sandboxed emulation adds to a strong deterministic validator when detecting misconfigurations in LLM-generated network-configuration artifacts. Under a frozen paired-binary design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) we generated Npairs = 720 intent→configuration tasks with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one model generation shared between the paired conditions) using the declared model gpt-5-mini. Conditions: (A) baseline = deterministic validator-only (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and (B) guarded = validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation. Results (complete paired set): baseline detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded detected 720/720 = 1.0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest for power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points); the observed effect is far below that threshold, indicating the study was not powered to detect such a vanishingly small aggregate difference. We report the preregistered design choices, exact archived sampling settings, and limitations that bound external generalization.

sections.introduction: Generative models that translate operator intent into executable network configuration are increasingly proposed as NetOps/AIOps components. Operational safety for such agentic workflows depends on the surrounding tooling—validators, verifiers, sandboxed execution, and guarded orchestration—rather than the LLM alone [1], [2]. Prior work advocates generate→validate→repair pipelines and prototype sandboxed validation, but quantitative cross-vendor evaluations of how much runtime emulation adds beyond a strong static validator are limited [2], [3]. We therefore preregistered and executed a focused paired confirmatory experiment to answer the operational question: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired-binary experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) executed end-to-end; (2) an artifact-grounded quantitative result on Npairs=720 showing a negligible aggregate guarded benefit in this setting; (3) a discussion of explanatory factors, threats to validity, and operational implications.
sections.related_work: Surveys and system papers report growing use of LLMs for intent-driven configuration and emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—deterministic validators, formal verifiers, and sandboxed emulation—to reduce operational risk [1], [2], [3]. Tool papers from adjacent domains show that verification and emulate-and-test approaches can locate runtime failures not captured by static rules, and several NetOps prototypes export generated artifacts to emulators (Mininet/other harnesses) or use configuration-analysis tools to increase confidence before execution [3]. Empirical studies of LLM behavior in configuration and code-generation domains report frequent incorrect outputs and note that external verifiers substantially reduce error prevalence; however, those studies also highlight wide variation across tasks, validators, and models and call for targeted, workflow-centred benchmarks [2], [4]. Our experiment operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of these recommendations by measuring marginal guarded-stage detection gain against a strong deterministic validator on a synthetic task bank.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. The study preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e; preregistration SHA-256 reported in the Disclosure) was frozen before execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial LLM generation shared across both conditions), Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks, planned episodes = 1440, and primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used in power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points) with a target ≈80% power under conservative baseline-rate assumptions; this is the design sensitivity and is explicitly reported here because the observed effect is much smaller (see Results). Task bank and inclusion. Confirmatory tasks were synthetic intent→configuration items (intent_configuration_repair_v1 family) covering abstracted vendor-CLI families and a small set of topology templates; inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance per the preregistration. Model and sampling. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry: openai_responses). Execution settings archived: max_output_tokens = 2000; temperature = null (unset) — the latter means we did not impose a client-side sampling temperature and therefore do not claim deterministic model sampling. Execution accounting: maximum_model_calls planned = 1440; model_calls_used = 721 (shared initial generations 720 plus one repair-stage call). Validator and guarded pipeline. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Guarded pipeline = deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation that can observe runtime behaviors not expressible in static rules. Missingness, repairs, and analysis. The preregistered missingness plan allowed deterministic reseeds for parser failures (up to two attempts) and deterministic replacement rules for irrecoverable technical failures; the confirmatory run recorded no irrecoverable exclusions and followed the preregistered repair/missingness policies. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and reported an exact McNemar two-sided test plus a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). All prompts, responses, validator traces, emulation outputs, and analysis artifacts were archived as specified in the preregistration.
sections.results: Confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Missingness and preregistration compliance: complete_pair_count = 720; there were no exclusions, no preregistration deviations recorded for the confirmatory analysis, and analysis artifacts (paired contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap parameters) are archived. Interpretation of inferential framing: the preregistered minimum detectable effect for which the study was powered was 0.20 (20 percentage points); the observed point estimate ≈0.0014 is far smaller than that design target and thus lies well below the originally planned sensitivity. Consequently, the lack of a substantial aggregated guarded benefit in this experiment should be interpreted in light of the studys design sensitivity and the task bank characteristics described below.
sections.discussion: Why was the guarded benefit negligible? Three explanatory factors supported by the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 achieved near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations present in the synthetic task bank, leaving little room for emulation to add detections; (2) curated, parser-valid tasks increase validator effectiveness compared with noisier, adversarial, or production inputs; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics ensured identical initial model outputs for both conditions, so discordance could only arise from guarded-stage emulation observations or the single recorded repair call (execution manifest records one repair-stage call). Operational implications. When a high-coverage static validator exists and the input tasks are well-matched to validator rules, adding sandboxed emulation may yield negligible marginal detection gains at the aggregate level. This finding does not imply sandboxed emulation is unnecessary: heterogeneous vendor behaviors, weaker validators, adversarial misconfigurations, large-scale stateful interactions, or production-scale topologies can create regimes where emulation provides substantial additional detection. Recommendations. Future work should evaluate broader and adversarial task banks, multiple model and validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation that better approximates vendor/OS nuances and scale effects to identify regimes where guarded pipelines materially improve operational safety.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator against the same validator augmented with automated sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated over 720 paired tasks, the guarded pipeline yielded a negligible absolute detection gain (0.0013889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. The result reflects a likely ceiling effect for the task bank and validator used and must be interpreted in light of the preregistered power target (minimum detectable effect = 0.20). We release artifact-grounded analysis and recommend targeted follow-up studies that expand task diversity, incorporate adversarial misconfigurations, and compare multiple validator and model families to map operational regimes where sandboxed execution adds substantive value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier or adversarial inputs.
Single model family (declared/requested: gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.
Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) constrain discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to production vendor/OS behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; scale and vendor nuances may change outcomes.

The study was powered for a preregistered minimum detectable effect of 0.20 (20 percentage points). The observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity; absence of a large aggregated guarded benefit in this experiment does not imply the guarded pipeline is never valuable in other operational regimes.
